claims.text: Ovarian supports: the mesovarium connects the ovaries to the broad ligament; the suspensory ligament carries the ovarian blood and lymph vessels; the ovarian ligament attaches the ovary to the uterus.
claims.quote: The ovaries are located within the pelvic cavity, and are supported by the mesovarium, an extension of the peritoneum that connects the ovaries to the broad ligament. Extending from the mesovarium itself is the suspensory ligament that contains the ovarian blood and lymph vessels. Finally, the ovary itself is attached to the uterus via the ovarian ligament.

claims.text: Broad ligament: a peritoneal fold that is a primary support of the uterus, attaching it to the pelvic wall.
claims.quote: The broad ligament is a fold of peritoneum that serves as a primary support for the uterus, extending laterally from both sides of the uterus and attaching it to the pelvic wall.

claims.text: Uterine tubes: the distal infundibulum ends in fimbriae; fertilization often occurs in the ampulla.
claims.quote: The wide distal infundibulum flares out with slender, finger-like projections called fimbriae. The middle region of the tube, called the ampulla, is where fertilization often occurs.

claims.text: Open-ended tubes: infection can ascend from the vagina through the uterus and tubes into the pelvic cavity.
claims.quote: The open-ended structure of the uterine tubes can have significant health consequences if bacteria or other contagions enter through the vagina and move through the uterus, into the tubes, and then into the pelvic cavity.

claims.text: Uterus: fundus above the tubal openings, body in the middle, and the cervix projecting into the vagina.
claims.quote: The portion of the uterus superior to the opening of the uterine tubes is called the fundus. The middle section of the uterus is called the body of uterus (or corpus). The cervix is the narrow inferior portion of the uterus that projects into the vagina.

claims.text: Uterine wall: the perimetrium is the outer serous layer; the myometrium is the thick smooth muscle layer responsible for contractions.
claims.quote: The most superficial layer is the serous membrane, or perimetrium, which consists of epithelial tissue that covers the exterior portion of the uterus. The middle layer, or myometrium, is a thick layer of smooth muscle responsible for uterine contractions.

claims.text: Endometrium: the innermost layer of the uterus.
claims.quote: The innermost layer of the uterus is called the endometrium.

claims.text: Stratum basalis: the endometrial layer next to the myometrium; it does not shed during menses.
claims.quote: The stratum basalis layer is part of the lamina propria and is adjacent to the myometrium; this layer does not shed during menses.

claims.text: Ovarian artery: a branch of the abdominal aorta that supplies the ovary, uterine tube and uterus.
claims.quote: Ovarian artery Branch of the abdominal aorta; supplies blood to ovary, uterine (Fallopian) tube, and uterus
claims.locator: Table: Vessels of the Abdominal Aorta

claims.text: Internal iliac artery: supplies the bladder, pelvic walls and external genitalia, and in females also the uterus and vagina.
claims.quote: Internal iliac artery Branch from the common iliac arteries; supplies blood to the urinary bladder, walls of the pelvis, external genitalia, and the medial portion of the femoral region; in females, also provides blood to the uterus and vagina
claims.locator: Table: Vessels of the Abdominal Aorta
